answers.working:
In Nyāya logic, the **anupasaṁhārī** (non-exclusive) form of the inconclusive middle term (savyabhicāra hetu) arises when the subject covers everything, so there is no example outside it against which the middle term can be checked. 'All things are non-eternal, because they are knowable' is the standard example: 'all things' leaves no positive or negative instance outside the subject.

The other options are different fallacies: 'The hill has fire because it is knowable' has a too-general middle term (sādhāraṇa); 'Fire is cold because it is a substance' is contradicted by perception (bādhita); 'Sound is eternal because it is produced' has a contradictory middle term (viruddha), since what is produced is non-eternal.

So the answer is option (A).
